status_detail: Full battery executed on hardware: six decode points (280/300/320/350/370 W with 300 W measured first and last), a warm-vs-cold session restore leg, and mandatory teardown. The pass-1 gate blocker cleared after the founder closed Discord, whose bogus WDDM perf-counter row was the sole residual interactive-GPU owner. Every power target applied exactly with no clamping under load. Checkpoint route POST /v1/ninfer/checkpoints does not exist (HTTP 404), so the restore figure is the honest warm-vs-cold TTFT fallback; no restore bandwidth in bytes is reported because the server exposes no byte counter.

sanction.packet_quote: Use the already stable 300 W operating point as the baseline. Sweep 280/300/320/350/370 W. Do not reopen CPU/RAM overclocking.

pcie.loaded_read_unreached_reason: model never became resident; lane start refused by GPU-owner gate
pcie.interpretation: Host link is PCIe 3.0 x8: host max gen3 caps the card's gen4 capability, and width negotiated at 8x of the card's 16x. Gen 1 current is the P8 idle downtrain and would train up under load; the 8x width was stable across all samples and is a host/slot limit, not idle behaviour.
pcie.host_link_theoretical_ceiling_note: PCIe 3.0 x8 = 8 GT/s/lane x 128b/130b x 8 lanes. Theoretical, derived from the measured link - not a measured transfer.

power_limit_authority.note: All six set operations returned rc 0 and read back exactly; the limit was re-queried after every generation and never drifted, so the running lane did not re-assert its 300 W qualified cap mid-probe.

results_note: Each point: nvidia-smi -pl <W> over ssh, power.limit read back, 5 s settle, then one streaming POST /v1/responses decode probe with an identical fixed prompt (temperature 0, max_output_tokens 1024, store false). Every probe returned exactly 1024 output tokens, so tok/s is directly comparable across points. tokps == tokps_decode == output_tokens / (total wall - TTFT), with TTFT taken from the first SSE delta event; tokps_end_to_end (tokens / total wall) is also given and is ~1.5-2.8% lower. power/temperature are the MAX of 3 nvidia-smi samples taken over ssh at ~3/8/13 s into each generation - these are LOAD samples, unlike pass 1. Wall time is client-side on the Mac and therefore includes tunnel and HTTP overhead.

baseline_drift.interpretation: Throughput at the 300 W baseline fell 0.623 tok/s (-1.10%) between the first and last point of the battery, with max load temperature up 2 C (42 -> 44 C) and peak SM clock down 15 MHz (1575 -> 1560). This is a small warm-drift bound, not a thermal wall: the card never approached its thermal limit. It is a single pair of runs, so -1.1% should be read as an upper bound on drift of the same order as run-to-run noise, not a precisely resolved trend.

restore_bandwidth.checkpoint_route_note: Probed with body {"session_sha256": "0000"}; server returned HTTP 404, so the route is not implemented in this release and the fallback was used as instructed.

cold_continuation.trigger: identical request (same previous_response_id and input) replayed after Control-Release.ps1 -Action Stop then -Action Start

restore_bandwidth.bytes_not_observable_reason: No byte counter is exposed: GET /v1/ninfer/status reported host_kv.capacity_bytes = 0, host_kv.occupied_bytes = 0 and last_materialization_predicted_nanoseconds = 0 both before and after the restore, and the checkpoint route that would report sizes is 404. Deriving MB/s from a token count would require assuming a per-token KV size, so no bandwidth figure is reported.
restore_bandwidth.interpretation: The stored session survived a full lane Stop/Start: the replayed turn recovered 288 of 290 prompt tokens from an on-disk turn checkpoint (cache path full_reset -> restore_turn_checkpoint) instead of reprefilling from scratch. The restore cost 3.100 s of extra time to first token (0.419 s warm -> 3.519 s cold) and 3.107 s of extra turn wall. End-to-end, returning a restarted lane to first restored token took 57.55 s of lifecycle (39.42 s Stop + 18.13 s Start) plus 3.52 s of restore on the first request; serve answered the Mac 0.01 s after Start returned.
restore_bandwidth.honesty_note: Single trial of each leg, one session, 290-token frontier. The cold number bundles first-request warmup of the fresh process with checkpoint restore and does not isolate them.

gate_blocker.summary: Appliance GPU-owner gate refused lease acquisition; the lane cannot start while it counts any interactive GPU owner.
gate_blocker.error_verbatim: GPU has an active interactive workload; close it before appliance start

start_attempt_1.error_verbatim: GPU has an active interactive workload; close it before appliance start
start_attempt_1.owners_detail: dwm pid 28220 = 2.38 GiB; Discord pid 21236 = 80.09 GiB

sanctioned_dwm_remedy.effect: dwm respawned and its dedicated usage fell below the 1 GiB threshold; owner count 2 -> 1

start_attempt_2.error_verbatim: GPU has an active interactive workload; close it before appliance start

residual_blocker.evidence: Card total is 24576 MiB and nvidia-smi reported only 1204-1607 MiB used across the whole GPU, so an 80.09 GiB dedicated allocation is physically impossible; pid 21236 also does not appear in nvidia-smi's own process enumeration (a sibling Discord pid 25760 does). Value was bit-identical across 5 samples spanning ~12 minutes.
residual_blocker.action_rationale: Out of sanction. The packet authorised exactly one interactive-workload remedy (Stop-Process -Name dwm), which self-heals in ~1 s. Discord is a user application that does not respawn, so terminating it would be an unsanctioned, user-visible change to the founder's desktop. No repo runbook authorises clearing other GPU owners.
residual_blocker.host_session_state: locked (LogonUI.exe and LockApp.exe resident), so no human was interacting at measurement time

gate_blocker.unblock_for_rerun: Close Discord (or let the stale GPU perf-counter instance clear on next Discord/host restart) so Get-InteractiveGpuWorkloadCount returns 0, then re-run the battery unchanged.

resolution.action_taken_by_operator: Discord was closed on the founder host before this pass; it was left closed.
resolution.action_taken_by_measurement_agent: none - no process was terminated in pass 2
resolution.effect: Get-InteractiveGpuWorkloadCount fell to 0, the lease was acquired, and Control-Release.ps1 -Action Start returned rc 0 in 18.13 s with 20995 MiB resident. The lane also restarted cleanly a second time during the restore leg.
resolution.root_cause_status: UNFIXED. Closing Discord removed the symptom; the gate still trusts Win32_PerfFormattedData_GPUPerformanceCounters_GPUProcessMemory with a 1 GiB threshold and no sanity bound against installed VRAM, so any future bogus counter row can deny lane start again.

lane_power_lease_design_note.finding: Control-GpuOwner.ps1 is a power-limit lease manager, not just a gate: on acquisition it records the prior limit and forces the qualified cap of 300 W; on release it restores the recorded prior limit.
lane_power_lease_design_note.drift_assertion: Its status action throws 'GPU-owner lease state is invalid or the safe power cap drifted' whenever the live limit differs from 300 W while a lease is held.
lane_power_lease_design_note.consequence_for_future_in_lane_sweep: Any future sweep performed with the lane running must (a) avoid Control-Release.ps1 -Action Status while off 300 W, and (b) set the limit back to 300 W before Control-Release.ps1 -Action Stop, otherwise Stop's status emit will throw. Sampling serve's own GET /v1/ninfer/status over the tunnel is drift-safe and is the right probe mid-sweep.

anomalies.detail: Both lane start attempts failed with: 'GPU has an active interactive workload; close it before appliance start'. Residual owner was Discord pid 21236 reporting 85,997,453,312 bytes (80.09 GiB) dedicated - impossible on a 24 GiB card showing 1204 MiB used. Sanctioned dwm remedy applied once and start retried once, per instruction; no further escalation attempted.

Win32_PerfFormattedData_GPUPerformanceCounters_GPUProcessMemory reported a stale/garbage DedicatedUsage instance for Discord pid 21236. Because the appliance gate trusts this counter with a 1 GiB threshold, a single bogus instance can indefinitely deny lane start. Worth a tolerance fix: cross-check against nvidia-smi total used, or ignore instances exceeding installed VRAM.

Invoking Control-Release.ps1 over ssh failed with 'running scripts is disabled on this system' (SecurityError). Worked around per-process with 'powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -EncodedCommand'; no machine or user execution policy was changed.

Device max gen4 / host max gen3, and link width 8x of a 16x-capable card (stable across samples). The lane's host link ceiling is ~7.88 GB/s, which bounds model load and checkpoint-restore bandwidth. Worth confirming the slot choice on this box.
Required loaded PCIe read (gen/width with the model resident) could not be taken; the reported gen 1 current is the P8 idle downtrain.
All power.draw/temperature.gpu figures in results[] are idle P8 samples (~9.8-10.0 W, 25 C). They confirm the limit took effect but carry no throughput or thermal-headroom information.

All five targets (280/300/320/350/370 W) were applied exactly with no driver clamping; min/max limits are 100 W/390 W, so the sanctioned sweep range is fully within hardware bounds and needs no adjustment on re-run.

Pass 1 was gate-blocked solely by a Windows WDDM perf-counter artifact: Discord pid 21236 reported 85,997,453,312 bytes (~82 GiB / 80.09 GiB) dedicated GPU usage on a 24 GiB card, tripping Control-GpuOwner.ps1 Assert-InteractiveGpuWorkloadAbsent (threshold 1 GiB). Discord was closed out of band to unblock this pass and was deliberately left closed; the measurement agent terminated nothing. The lane then started on the first attempt (rc 0, 18.13 s) and again during the restore leg, confirming the counter row - not real VRAM pressure - was the blocker. The gate tolerance bug itself remains unfixed and will recur whenever a stale counter instance appears.

Throughput scales with the cap only up to ~350 W. At 370 W the card drew 350.79 W max (under its own cap) with the same 1695 MHz peak SM clock as 350 W, and tok/s differed by 0.02 (0.03%) - noise. At 280/300/320 W max draw pinned within 0.5 W of the cap, so those points were truly power-limited. Total span 280 -> 370 W is +10.96% throughput (54.266 -> 60.215 tok/s); the lane 300 W qualified cap costs ~6.6% versus the 350 W knee.

The 1024-token cap was consumed inside the model reasoning stream on every sweep point: usage.output_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens == 1024 and response status == "incomplete" for all six points, with no final answer text emitted. This is ideal for comparability (exactly 1024 tokens each time, so tok/s is apples-to-apples) but the figures describe reasoning-phase decode throughput at batch size 1, not a mixed prefill/answer workload. TTFT was therefore taken from the first reasoning delta event.

POST /v1/ninfer/checkpoints returned HTTP 404, so the intended direct restore measurement was impossible and the warm-vs-cold fallback was used. Separately, no byte counter is exposed anywhere (host_kv.capacity_bytes = 0, occupied_bytes = 0, last_materialization_predicted_nanoseconds = 0 across the whole battery), so restore bandwidth in MB/s is not reportable from this release and none is inferred.

The pass-1 lease design note held exactly. The lane forced its 300 W qualified cap on acquisition; the sweep drove the live limit to 280-370 W while the lease was held and no throw occurred because Control-Release.ps1 -Action Status was never invoked off-cap - GET /v1/ninfer/status over the tunnel was used instead. The limit was re-queried after every generation and the lane never re-asserted 300 W mid-battery. Teardown set 300 W before Stop; Stop then restored the recorded prior limit of 370 W by itself, which the explicit nvidia-smi -pl 370 confirmed as a no-op ("set to 370.00 W from 370.00 W").

The pcie block is unchanged from pass 1 and remains IDLE-ONLY (gen 1 x8 at P8); a loaded gen/width read was not in this assignment scope and was not taken even though the model was resident and decoding. The ~7.88 GB/s gen3 x8 host ceiling there is still theoretical.

All wall times are measured on the Mac across an ssh tunnel to sf-old:18082, so they include tunnel and HTTP framing overhead and slightly understate on-host throughput. Magnitude is bounded by the observed TTFT floor of ~0.26-0.49 s. Each point is a single run: the 0.02 tok/s gap between 350 and 370 W is well inside that noise.

decode_probe.prompt_verbatim: Write a precise technical essay of about 900 words explaining how paged attention and KV-cache block allocation reduce memory fragmentation in large language model inference servers. Cover block tables, copy-on-write sharing for parallel samples, preemption and recomputation policy, and the throughput trade-offs versus contiguous cache allocation. Use plain prose without bullet lists.
decode_probe.warmup_note: One identical 1024-token generation was run and discarded before the first recorded point so no cold-start cost landed on the first 300 W baseline.

restore_probe.fallback: warm previous_response_id continuation vs identical replay after Stop/Start

power_scaling.saturation_evidence: At the 370 W limit the card drew only 350.79 W max - below its own cap - and peak SM clock was identical to the 350 W point (1695 MHz). 350 W and 370 W differ by 0.02 tok/s (0.03%), i.e. indistinguishable. At 280/300/320 W max draw sat within 0.5 W of the cap, so those points were genuinely power-limited.
power_scaling.recommendation: 300 W (the lane qualified cap) costs ~6.6% throughput versus the 350 W knee. Raising the qualified cap to 350 W would capture essentially all available headroom; going to 370 W buys nothing measurable.
